findings.text: _queued_authority returns None on CrewError or OSError and node_context_fit_finding then measures anyway with authority=None, so a landing fragment the dispatch grants is charged as a load and an entry its own launch would admit can be refused at queue time; the docstring's claim that an unresolvable authority is left to the checks that own that refusal is not what the code does.

_request_lane restates the queue writer's lane-precedence expression at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:313-315 instead of extending it, so a future change to how a request resolves its lane would be measured under one rule here and stored under another.

_QueuedLane is an undeclared structural stand-in for DispatchPlan passed to a parameter annotated DispatchPlan; a field the fit verdict later reads but this class does not carry raises inside _queue_batch rather than failing where the stand-in is built.
